newsitem.title: USA: U.S. heating oil extends consolidation on ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. heating oil extends consolidation on ACCESS.

text.p: U.S. heating oil futures continued to fall in thin after-hours trading on Thursday, after two days of steep gains ended in a late day-session retreat.
Following a two-cent gain on Wednesday, and new highs of 72.80 cents early today, October heating oil settled at 70.90 cents a gallon, down 0.87 cent.
Traders saw further consolidation on Friday, with most majors forecast to be out of the market ahead of the weekend.
"I see choppy trading...with no volume," one after-hours trader said.
Support for October heating oil, which expires September 30, is seen at 70 cents on Friday, with a cap at 71 cents.
Heating oil traded 70.60 cents a gallon on early ACCESS, down 0.30 from the settle on 11 lots exchanged.
Meanwhile, front-month crude tracked heating oil's fall, with bids at $23.98 a barrel and offers at $24.03, after settling down 30 cents at $24.16.
October unleaded gasoline traded nearly unchanged at 63 cents a gallon, with a light 35 lots traded.
